blocks.text: Magnetic tape let early computers carry information between runs. But storage alone did not tell a programme whether coordinate values represented separate points, a connected road, a parcel boundary or an attribute table.

blocks.text: When assessing an early file, look for the structure around its coordinates: stable feature identifiers, rules for joining linework, attributes tied to geometry and a way to retrieve or edit the features together. A coordinate file could be valuable spatial data and still be only one input to a GIS.

blocks.text: New Zealand’s early digital geography came from several jobs developing at once. Chapter 3 follows computer cartography; Chapters 4 and 5 follow imagery and land inventories; Chapter 6 looks at systems that brought more of those functions together.
